A vibrant and nurturing independent preparatory school
The heart of everything we do
Be Kind, Work Hard
We strive to create an environment where kindness shapes interactions, and dedication fuels achievement. Through a rich curriculum, supportive pastoral care, and diverse extracurricular opportunities, we empower our pupils to develop the skills and character they need to thrive.

Meet Eldric!
Meet Eldric
Our School Mascot
At Gayhurst, our school philosophy — Enriching Learning, Developing Resilience, Independence and Confidence — inspired the creation of Eldric, our beloved school mascot.
Eldric is a baby Emperor penguin, chosen for his sociable nature, resilience, and teamwork — qualities we nurture in our pupils. He brings these values to life in a fun and meaningful way across the school.
Initially introduced to Nursery and Reception, each classroom has a large plush Eldric, offering comfort and familiarity. Each term, selected pupils who show exceptional independence, confidence or resilience are awarded their own Eldric as a special prize.
Eldric stars in Pre Prep assemblies, where MAGIC badges are awarded weekly to children who embody these qualities. On weekends, he continues his adventures with a Nursery or Reception pupil, staying connected to the Gayhurst family.
More than a mascot, Eldric is a symbol of the strength of character we aim to build in every child. Older pupils quickly embraced him, and now he’s a familiar face at school events — from birthday parties to Sports Day — spreading joy and reminding us of the values we hold dear.
ELDRIC encourges our children to be kind and work hard
In September 2025, following the opening of our new Sports Hall, Auditorium and Dance Studio earlier in the year, Gayhurst entered an exciting new chapter — and introduced the guiding phrase be kind work hard.
Leading the way was Eldric, our school mascot, proudly wearing his yellow wristband as a daily reminder that at the heart of Gayhurst, and central to all we do, is #BeKindWorkHard.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Governors | Governance at Gayhurst School
pageCache.text:
Our People: Governors
We work together with one shared purpose
Provide the very best for our children
The Full Governing Board and each of its committees, Education, Marketing and Finance & General Purposes, meet termly but more frequently if required. Additional committees such as a Development Committee, are established as necessary. Additional non-voting members can be co-opted onto committees where specific skill sets are required for projects. The aim of the Full Governing Board of Gayhurst is to give each pupil an opportunity to achieve their potential in academic, cultural and sporting pursuits. The three committees support these aims and work towards the success of the school. The Full Board ratifies all decisions and policies reviewed by the three committees and considers all matters which do not fit within a specific committees’ terms of reference.
Our Governors
Mr W. Gibbs (Patron)
He is the grandson of Stormont Gibbs who bought the school in 1927 and moved it to its present site. He is married with two children and was educated at the school. His father was a previous Chairman of Governors. He currently lives in Ireland which he has represented at cricket
Mr R. Skinner (Chair)
Rob Skinner LLB Dip.PR FCIPR
With two journalists as parents, it was perhaps inevitable that Rob Skinner would be drawn to a career in media relations. He has 35 years’ experience as a PR leader and spokesperson for major British and international brands, including Nationwide Building Society, HSBC and PayPal.
Rob has spoken on crisis communications at industry conferences, reflecting his experience advising senior leaders on major issues over the decades. Rob is also a seasoned interviewee on television and radio – he once drove to a Gayhurst summer event directly from the Sky News studios.
Rob moved to Buckinghamshire from his native Wales in 2001, and lives with his family in Chalfont St Giles, including their lovely pet cavapoo. His son enjoyed eight happy years at Gayhurst before moving on to secondary school in 2019.
Rob enjoys cycling (he has twice cycled from Land’s End to John O’Groats), reading and history, and blogs at robskinner.net. He has also followed the fortunes of the Welsh rugby and football teams since his Cardiff childhood, which provided an early lesson that success cannot be taken for granted.
Mrs A. Borwick
Aneeta has practised as a solicitor for over 25 years and alongside this, following her appointment in 2009, sits part time as a Deputy District Judge.Aneeta is married with one son who had a very happy seven years at Gayhurst.
Outside of work, Aneeta enjoys running, cooking and watching her son play sports
Mrs G Fienberg
Mr N. Garner
Nick is an entrepreneur and digital marketing specialist. He is married with 2 children, both of whom attended Gayhurst School. His outside interests include property investment and supporting organisations who drive positive social change.
Ms E. Halliday
Elizabeth Halliday (aka Elizabeth Welch) FRICS (F&GP)
Elizabeth was a Director of Jones Lang LaSalle responsible for advising Corporate Companies for many years. More recently she has founded her own property consultancy company.
Prior to moving to Gerrards Cross her 2 boys were educated at a co-educational school in London and then they enjoyed attending Gayhurst. From there they both went to The Royal Grammar School and then on to read languages at University.
Her interests include playing tennis at Bull Lane, singing in the Village Voices Choir, quilting and she is learning to play saxophone.
Miss T. Hartley
Tracey Hartley is Headteacher at John Hampden Grammar School in High Wycombe. Prior to JHGS she was acting Headteacher at Nonsuch High School for Girls, a high performing girls Grammar School in the London Borough of Sutton. Outside of work Tracey’s interests are travelling, walking and going to the theatre.
Mrs S. Kerr
Selina Kerr, BA, MBA, Dip.Couns, MBACP
Mr G MacPhee
George MacPhee BA ACA BFP
George is a chartered accountant with over 5 years experience working in audit. George grew up in Gerrards Cross and attended Gayhurst School along with his brother Ben. He later attended Shiplake College and then Bournemouth University studying Business & Finance. He has also been on the steering committee of the Gayhurst alumni association. His father is also a previous governor at Gayhurst.
Mr S. Potts
Mr A. Wallace
Alex Wallace has been a Geography teacher for over 20 years. He studied at Birmingham University before completing his PGCE at Bath University. Alex has taught across all sectors of education during his career; state, grammar and independent.Alex began teaching in Oxfordshire, one of his early highlights was building an academic partnership with a school in Rwanda. He was part of several student and staff exchanges. Before joining Leighton Park, Alex was the Deputy Headmaster at The Royal Grammar School, High Wycombe. Here, he led the day to day running of school and the Teaching and Learning. This was where he also developed his relationship with Gayhurst School as he oversaw the transition between the two schools.During his time at RGS Alex also coached the Under 15 rugby side to the National Final at Twickenham.A keen sportsman himself, he has played both semi-professional rugby and cricket. As age has started to catch up on him, he is now more likely to be found with a golf club or tennis racket in hand!
Alex’s very first taste of teaching was in South Africa before university. It was also during this year that he met his wife, Amy. They now live at Leighton Park with their three children, George, Charlie and William.

Wraparound Care & Enrichment at Gayhurst School
the school day is full of opportunity
To support, inspire, and delight
At Gayhurst, we understand that busy family life needs flexibility—and we’re here to support you every step of the way. Our wraparound care is designed to make the school day work for you, while enriching your child’s experience beyond the classroom.
We offer a generous drop-off window each morning, giving parents the freedom to arrive at a time that suits them and helps avoid the inevitable traffic rush. For those needing extended hours, our Breakfast Club and Supper Club (available at an additional charge) provide a warm, welcoming start and end to the day, complete with nutritious meals and engaging activities.
All children from Nursery upwards enjoy a healthy, freshly prepared lunch included in the school fees. Our meals are more than just fuel—they’re an education in taste, encouraging children to explore new flavours and develop healthy eating habits for life.
After the school day ends, our free wind-down clubs run until 5.15pm, offering a relaxed and enjoyable space for children to unwind. In addition, we offer an extensive programme of termly clubs and activities for children from Reception to Year 6. These range from sports and music to coding, drama, and creative arts—ensuring every child has the opportunity to discover new interests and develop their talents.
Throughout the year, children also take part in a wide variety of school trips, designed to enhance their learning and open their eyes to the wider world. Whether it’s a museum visit, a nature walk, or a cultural experience, these outings are a vital part of our commitment to broad, balanced education.
At Gayhurst, the school day is full of opportunity—from morning to evening—and every moment is designed to support, inspire, and delight.

pageCache.text:
Nursery and Reception
welcome to
The Early Years Foundation Stage
The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) at Gayhurst is a joyful and nurturing journey that begins the September after children turn three. Over two years—Nursery and Reception—our youngest learners are gently guided through a rich, play-based curriculum that lays the foundation for a lifelong love of learning.
Our Nursery class welcomes up to 25 children and is led by a dedicated team of three experienced staff members. With a strong focus on personal development, communication, and curiosity, children thrive in a warm and stimulating environment where every child is known, valued, and encouraged to grow.
Reception is the natural next step, with children moving seamlessly from Nursery alongside new joiners. We offer three Reception classes, each capped at just 16 children to ensure individual attention and meaningful relationships. Every class is supported by a qualified teacher and a full-time teaching assistant, creating a calm and focused setting where children feel safe and confident to explore.
Specialist teaching enriches both Nursery and Reception, with weekly sessions in Spanish, Music, Computing, and Sport. In Reception, children also begin swimming lessons—an exciting milestone that builds confidence and physical development.
Our EYFS is designed to spark imagination, build resilience, and foster independence. Whether your child is taking their first steps into Nursery or joining us in Reception, they’ll be welcomed into a caring community where learning is joyful, friendships flourish, and every child is supported to shine.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our People | Dedicated Staff at Gayhurst School
pageCache.text:
Our People: Staff, Leadership & Governors
We work together with one shared purpose
Provide the very best for our children
At Gayhurst, our community is at the heart of everything we do. From our dedicated teaching staff to our senior leadership team and governors, every member of our school is carefully selected to embrace and uphold the values that make Gayhurst so special. We work together with one shared purpose: to provide the very best for our children. Each individual brings passion, expertise, and care to their role, ensuring that every child is supported, challenged, and known. We are also proud to work closely with the Gayhurst Parents’ Association (GPA)—a passionate and committed group of parents who support the school wholeheartedly and help foster the strong sense of community that defines us.
Senior Leadership Team
Mrs Amanda McKnight
head
Amanda began her career in PR and marketing before training as a teacher, and her career has taken her through both the UK and US education systems. She has worked in state and independent schools and helped establish a Reggio Emilia-inspired Early Childhood Centre in Chicago.
Most recently, Amanda was Head of Pre-Prep at Somerhill in Kent, where she was a member of the whole-school Senior Leadership Team and helped lead the school collectively during a period of interim leadership.
As both an educator and a parent of three grown-up children, Amanda understands the trust families place in a school and the importance of a strong partnership between home and school. She is a passionate advocate for non-selective prep education and believes that children develop at different rates. Her approach is rooted in knowing every child well, supporting them when they need help and stretching them when they are ready for more.
Amanda believes that academic ambition, exceptional pastoral care and a broad education should sit comfortably alongside one another, giving children the confidence, curiosity and strong foundations they need for the next stage of their lives.
Alongside her role at Gayhurst, Amanda is a Governor at Bethany School, an independent day and boarding school. Outside school, she enjoys spending time with family and friends, being outdoors and, by her own admission, is still learning how not to work all the time.
Mr David Bushnell
Deputy Head
Born in Watford and raised in Northwood, David has always had a strong passion for sport and lifelong learning. A scratch golfer and enthusiastic follower of Queen’s Park Rangers, he enjoys balancing his professional life with personal interests that keep him active and engaged. His great passion of cricket now takes somewhat of a backseat, although he still enjoys playing cricket occasionally and holds a Level 3 coaching award.
Before graduating with Qualified Teacher Status from London University, David spent 18 months working in IT in the city. He later specialised in primary education, spending five rewarding years at Davenies before joining Gayhurst in 2008 as Head of IT. His leadership journey continued as he became Deputy Head in January 2017.
David remains committed to education beyond the classroom. He has served as a Governor at his local primary school and the board of trustees at a local multi-academy trust. His current focus lies in mentoring, strategic leadership, and supporting educational development.
Away from Gayhurst, David enjoys time with his partner Sam, their son Stanley—who attends Gayhurst—and their Labrador, Percy.
Miss Melissa Legg
Assistant Head (Prep School) & Head of RS
Born in Oxford, Melissa moved to live and grow up in Saudi Arabia. She was educated within the American Grade school system until she returned to the UK to board full time in the Independent Schools system from the age of 9 until 16.
Melissa initially trained at Henley College to work within a Nursery setting and is a qualified Nursery Nurse. After a gap year working, she studied for a BEd (Hons) RS at Oxford and then went to work within the Independent School sector.
Melissa has worked in 4 different Preparatory schools in Buckinghamshire and Berkshire within the co-educational and single sex settings. Melissa arrived at Gayhurst in 2007 to take up the SLT position of Head of Middle School at Gayhurst which she held for 12 years before taking up the position of Assistant Head – Prep School in 2025. She is also Head of Religious Studies.
Melissa was part of the founding committee of the GHA and to be involved working the Alumni committee and is often the contact point for ex-pupils when they wish to visit or undertake work experience and is thrilled to work alongside the Development Office with this aspect of her role.
Mrs Wendy Cook
Assistant Head (Data, Assessment & Reporting) & Director of Digital Learning
Mrs Wendy Cook has built a distinguished career across preparatory schools in Buckinghamshire and Middlesex, working in both co-educational and all-girls settings. A specialist in Mathematics teaching, she completed her BEd (Hons) in Oxford before embarking on a career marked by innovation, leadership, and a deep commitment to pupils’ learning.
In the early part of her career, Mrs Cook also taught swimming and life-saving to both adults and children, reflecting her broad skill set and enthusiasm for supporting learners in diverse ways. She joined Gayhurst in 2017 as a Mathematics teacher and soon progressed to Director of Digital Learning and also interim Head of Mathematics. In 2022, Mrs Cook was appointed to the Senior Leadership Team as Assistant Head, with responsibility for data, assessment, and reporting.
Mrs Cook has a large and close-knit family, including four children—two of whom also work at Gayhurst—adding a meaningful personal connection to her professional life and she greatly enjoys spending time with her grandson.
Raised on a farm, she spent many hours helping out throughout her childhood, a commitment that still continues today. Her love of nature and animals—particularly dogs and chickens—remains a central part of her life. Beyond school and family, she enjoys puzzles, off-road driving, and the calm satisfaction of time spent outdoors.
Mrs Helen Williams
Assistant Head (Pre-Prep School)
Helen completed her primary school education in Buckinghamshire, before relocating with her family to Salisbury, where she attended South Wilts Grammar School For Girls.
Helen knew from an early age that she wished to be a teacher and on leaving school, completed a degree in education at the University of Exeter.
On completion of her university education, Helen returned to Buckinghamshire to take up her first teaching position at Caldicott, a local boarding school for boys. When her daughters were small, Helen taught part time at Dair House, before following her children to Maltman’s Green School, initially for six weeks supply work, before staying for six years.
Ten years ago, interested in working in a co-ed school, Helen joined Gayhurst as a part time Reception teacher. After five years, she moved across the field to Nursery with Mrs Dibble. This year, with her daughters both at university, Helen decided the time was right for a new personal challenge and is excited to take up her new role in Pre Prep School.
Mrs Vanessa Lakatos
Bursar
Based in Henley on Thames, Vanessa ran a successful retail business for 18 years. In 2014 she decided to have a change of career and joined The Cost Reduction Company who specialise in helping independent schools to “use less stuff”. After a couple of years Vanessa became bursar of Padworth College, Berkshire, a boarding school specialising in international students. Having managed the sale of the College to its new proprietors Vanessa joined the team at Gayhurst in 2019.
Outside of Gayhurst Vanessa is a Board member of the Independent School Bursars Association (ISBA), a Governor of a large primary school and a trustee of the Acorn Music Theatre Company.
Vanessa has 2 adult daughters and 2 dogs. The dogs, Polo and Echo, are usually to be found snoring under her desk at school.
Miss Michelle Upton
Director of Admissions & Marketing
Michelle was born and raised in Watford, where she attended Watford Grammar School for Girls. Her passion for education and communication led her to pursue a Marketing Diploma through The Centre for Marketing Schools in Australia, completed via distance learning.
Since joining Gayhurst in 2013, Michelle has brought a wealth of experience from her work in four independent schools, spanning single-sex and co-educational settings, as well as day and boarding environments. Her breadth of experience has shaped her strong belief in the value of co-education and the importance of nurturing inclusive school communities.
As Director of Marketing & Admissions, Michelle leads the school’s strategic marketing initiatives and oversees all aspects of the admissions process and takes particular pride in supporting first-time parents as they navigate independent education. She very much hopes her approachable manner helps families feel welcomed and quickly at home in the Gayhurst community.
Outside of work, Michelle is a proud mother of two adult daughters. Her three dogs are regular companions at school, adding a touch of warmth to the office atmosphere.
Michelle’s leisure time is spent immersed in lifelong learning and creative pursuits, reflecting her commitment to personal growth.

pageCache.text:
About Gayhurst School
a broad, rounded education
Strong Foundations, Wide Horizons
Founded in 1908, Gayhurst is a long-established, forward-thinking and proudly co-educational prep school for children aged 3 to 11. Set within beautiful grounds on the edge of Gerrards Cross, surrounded by fields and woodland yet within easy reach of London, the school gives children the space and freedom to explore, create and grow.
A Gayhurst education combines academic ambition with exceptional pastoral care and a rich breadth of opportunity. Children enjoy a varied curriculum that extends far beyond the classroom, encompassing sport, music, drama, art, technology and the natural world.
Boys and girls have been learning and growing alongside one another at Gayhurst for nearly two decades. They learn to listen to different perspectives, respect one another and develop the empathy and understanding they will need in the world beyond school. For families, there is also something particularly special about brothers and sisters sharing the same school, traditions and memories.
Gayhurst pupils are exceptionally well prepared for the next stage of their education, progressing to a wide range of senior schools, including leading independent and grammar schools. They leave with strong foundations, wide horizons and the confidence to embrace whatever comes next

Our Vision, Aims and Ethos
we want our children to be happy
Our Vision, Aims & Ethos
At Gayhurst, our vision is rooted in joy, inclusivity, and opportunity. We offer the broadest possible education so that every child can experience as much as possible—academically, creatively, socially, and emotionally. Above all, we want our children to be happy. We believe that when children feel safe, valued, and excited to learn, they thrive.
We are proud of our diverse and welcoming community. Our pupils come from a wide range of backgrounds, abilities, faiths, and learning needs, and we celebrate each child as an individual. Our ethos—Every child known, every talent grown—guides everything we do. We help children discover their strengths, explore new interests, and build the confidence to take their next steps with clarity and enthusiasm.
Vision
Empowering children to discover their passions, take risks and thrive – within a kind, connected and supportive community.
Aims of the School
By the time our children leave us, they’ve had a wealth of experiences, discovered where their passions lie, and built memories they’ll carry with them forever. Learning at Gayhurst is not just about preparation—it’s about inspiration, belonging, and fun.

pageCache.text:
Safeguarding
safeguarding
Promoting the welfare of pupils
Gayhurst School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of young people and expects all staff, visitors and volunteers to share this commitment.
We believe that students have a right to learn in a supportive, caring and safe environment, which includes the right to protection from all types of abuse, where staff are vigilant for signs of any student in need and are confident about applying the processes to avert and alleviate any such problems. We have a Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy and procedures in place; these can be viewed on our website in the Policies section. All staff (including supply staff, volunteers and Governors) must ensure that they are aware of these procedures.
Mr Ben StevensonDirector of Digital LearningSafeguarding Coordinator
Mr David BushnellActing HeadDesignated Safeguarding Lead (DSL)
Mrs Helen WilliamsAssistant Head, Pre-PrepDeputy Safeguarding Lead
Safeguarding is about ensuring that everyone is safe from harm – safe from bullying, safe from people who could abuse, safe from discrimination or harassment – and that we all feel safe in our environment.
On occasions, we may need to share information and work in partnership with other agencies when there are concerns about a young person’s welfare. We will ensure that concerns about our students are discussed first with his/her parents/carers unless we have reason to believe that this would be contrary to their welfare.
If your child is ever concerned about safety or well-being or about a friend, they should talk to one of the school’s Designated Safeguarding Team.
To email our Safeguarding Team, please do so here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Head | Gayhurst Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Head
A Very Warm Welcome to Gayhurst
When parents choose a school, they are entrusting it with far more than their child’s education; they are entrusting it with a precious part of their childhood. As both a mother of three and an educator, I never lose sight of the significance of that trust.
The prep school years should be filled with happiness, curiosity and adventure. Children have only one childhood, and there should be no rush to move them through it. They need time to play, explore, laugh with friends, make mistakes, try again and discover what makes them light up. I want Gayhurst children to arrive each morning excited about the day ahead and to go home with stories to tell.
Of course, we want children to love learning and achieve highly. But education is not simply about the results they collect; it is also about the people they become along the way. At Gayhurst, academic ambition and exceptional pastoral care go hand in hand. Children learn best when they feel happy, secure and understood, and when they know that the adults around them believe in them and are firmly on their side.
At Gayhurst, we are ambitious for every child. Children develop in different ways and at different times, and part of the privilege of these years is helping each one discover what they are capable of. Success may be found in a classroom or laboratory, on a sports field or stage, through music or art, or in the quiet courage it takes to put up a hand, try something new or have another go.
Our motto, Be Kind, Work Hard, reflects the balance at the heart of Gayhurst. We want children to leave us with strong academic foundations, but also with curiosity, resilience, kindness and
confidence. We want them to remember not only what they achieved, but the friendships they made, the interests they discovered and the people who helped them believe in themselves. Most importantly, we want them to be comfortable in their own skin and excited about the learning and opportunities still ahead of them.
From the moment I first came to Gayhurst, I was struck by its warmth and the genuine sense of belonging that runs through the school. This is a community where children are truly known, families are valued and people look out for one another. It is a very special place, and I feel enormously privileged to be the first female Head in Gayhurst’s long history and to lead this incredible school into its next chapter.
The best way to understand Gayhurst is to experience it for yourself. I would be delighted to welcome you, have a cup of tea together and hear about your child: who they are, what makes them smile and what you hope their school years will give them.
Amanda McKnightHead of Gayhurst

Frequently Asked Questions
FAQs
Children can join our Nursery from the age of 3 (the September following their 3rd birthday). We welcome new pupils into all year groups, subject to availability and suitability.
Yes, all children are invited to spend time at the school during a relaxed assessment visit (Years 1 to 6) or an activity session (Nursery & Reception). This helps us understand their individual needs and ensure they will thrive in our environment.
We pride ourselves on small class sizes, allowing for personalised attention and strong relationships between pupils and staff. We aim for 16 per class in the Pre Prep and 18 per class in the Prep School
We offer a broad and balanced curriculum that goes beyond the National Curriculum, designed to challenge academically while nurturing creativity, confidence, and curiosity.
Yes, we provide Breakfast Club from early morning and after-school care until 17:15, with an optional Supper Club available until 18:00. Breakfast and Supper Club have a small additional charge.
Yes, all children receive a freshly prepared, nutritionally balanced lunch, and snacks are provided at the end of the day for those attending after-school activities. Nursery children have a mid-morning snack provided by us and we allow the children in the older years to bring in their own healthy snack – a small independent step they all thoroughly enjoy.
We offer a wide range of clubs and activities, most of which are included in the fees. These cover sports, music, arts, languages, and more.
Pastoral care is at the heart of everything we do at Gayhurst. We ensure every child feels known, supported, and valued through strong relationships and a caring school culture. In the Pre Prep, most classes benefit from dedicated Teaching Assistants, while in the Prep School, each form is supported by an assistant form teacher and a team of support staff placed where they’re most needed. We also offer additional wellbeing support through our school counsellor and a dedicated Wellbeing Hub, providing a safe and nurturing space for children to talk, reflect, and grow.
Absolutely. We offer personal tours every day of the week and Open Events throughout the year. You’re welcome to visit as many times as you wish. Visit the booking page.
Once you’ve visited, you can register your child online. We’ll then arrange a visit and assessment, after which the Head will review all information before making an offer.
Homework is introduced gradually and appropriately for each age group. It is designed to reinforce learning, encourage independence, and support good study habits without overwhelming children or families.
Yes, we provide tailored support for children who may need additional help, as well as extension activities for those who benefit from further academic challenge. Our aim is to meet each child’s individual needs.
Mobile phones are not permitted during the school day to ensure a focused and balanced environment. Digital learning is carefully integrated into the curriculum from Nursery. Personal devices are introduced at year 4.
We believe strong communication between home and school is key to every child’s success. Parents are kept well-informed through regular newsletters, parent-teacher meetings, and our secure online portal. Our active Parents’ Association (GPA) works closely with the school, and through their class representative initiative, they meet regularly with senior staff to share feedback, ask questions, and discuss all aspects of school life.
The school day begins with arrival from 08:00, with drop-off available until 08:40.
The end of the day is staggered, starting at 15:00 for Nursery and finishing at 16:25 for Year 6.
After-school activities run until 16:15 for Pre Prep and 17:15 for Prep pupils.
We offer flexible after-school care with collection options at both 16:15 and 17:15, making it easier for families with children in different year groups.
Wraparound care is available to all pupils, starting with Breakfast Club from 07:30 and ending with Supper Club at 18:00.
The Term Dates are located on the Fees and Bursaries Page
If you have any other questions about Gayhurst, please contact and we’ll always be happy to help
